steps.content: Starting with a Random Forest Classifier with a moderate number of estimators and depth to establish a baseline performance.

The Random Forest model achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.96481 with a standard deviation of 0.01857. The validation accuracy is 0.94737. This is a good baseline, but I will continue to explore variations to improve accuracy further.
Increasing the number of estimators to see if it improves model performance, while keeping the depth the same to maintain complexity.

The model with 200 estimators resulted in a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95978, which is lower than the previous configuration. The validation accuracy remained the same at 0.94737. This indicates that increasing the number of estimators did not improve performance. I will try a different approach by adjusting the maximum depth instead.
Testing a deeper tree by increasing the max depth, which may capture more complex patterns in the data.

The model with a maximum depth of 15 resulted in the same mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.96481 and validation accuracy of 0.94737 as the initial configuration. There is no improvement, so I will explore a different model type for comparison.
Switching to a Gradient Boosting Classifier as it may capture the data's structure better with its boosting mechanism.

The Gradient Boosting model achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.94725 with a validation accuracy of 0.94737, which is lower than the best Random Forest configuration. Thus, switching to Gradient Boosting did not yield better results. I will try increasing the learning rate and depth to see if that improves performance.
Increasing the max depth and adjusting the learning rate to allow the model to capture more complex patterns and learn more effectively.

The Gradient Boosting model with increased max depth and learning rate resulted in significantly lower mean cross-validated accuracy (0.92975) and validation accuracy (0.90643) compared to previous experiments. This indicates overfitting or inappropriate parameter choices. I will return to Random Forest and try a different combination of hyperparameters.
Returning to the Random Forest model and adjusting the number of estimators and max depth to find a more optimal configuration.

The Random Forest model with 150 estimators and a max depth of 12 achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95978 and a validation accuracy of 0.94737. This configuration does not improve upon the best result so far. Since further improvements are unlikely, I will stop here.

steps.final_recommendation: The best model is the Random Forest with 100 estimators and max depth of 10, achieving a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.96481 and validation accuracy of 0.94737.
